claim.purpose: Allow typed lifecycle metadata commits without masking substantive review drift

initial.title: [v0.91.7][csdlc-v2][publish] Avoid stale review loop after publication metadata commit
initial.goal: Permit approved typed lifecycle metadata commits after review without weakening substantive review guards.
initial.required_outcome: A reviewed publication remains publishable after a commit containing only recognized C-SDLC lifecycle metadata, while source changes still require re-review.
authority_boundary: Only bounded C-SDLC metadata paths qualify for automatic non-substantive proof
Substantive repository paths remain review-authority controlled
Merged-publication reconciliation retains exact remote identity checks
initial.task_boundary: Classify typed publication metadata commits and preserve fail-closed substantive drift behavior.
deliverables: Regression tests for publication metadata and substantive drift
acceptance_criteria: Recognized lifecycle metadata commits do not stale a clean review
Malformed explicit proof remains fail closed
initial.plan_summary: Define safe lifecycle metadata paths, derive automatic proof only for metadata-only commit transitions, and prove source drift remains blocked.

steps.action: Define and implement bounded lifecycle metadata classification
Integrate automatic metadata-only proof into repository review guard
Add #4641-style regression proof and validate merged guard behavior

invariants: Only explicit recognized lifecycle metadata paths are non-substantive
A source or retained-design change cannot pass automatic proof
Explicit malformed proof cannot be upgraded by automatic classification
risks: Over-broad metadata paths could mask real work
Publication commits can touch several generated card surfaces
Revision parsing must remain exact and commit-bound

validation_lanes.proof_role: review/publication stale-loop regression and fail-closed source drift

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on unknown paths, malformed proof, revision mismatch, or substantive changes.
review_prompts: Can a source or retained-design change bypass review?
Are all normal typed publication metadata surfaces covered without allowing arbitrary files?
Does merged reconciliation still require exact identity and final reviewed intent?
